newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW clears Viscoplast shares for trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW clears Viscoplast shares for trade.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has approved for public trade shares in the Viscoplast SA adhesive bandage maker, whose initial public offering starts in January, the KPW's head said on Friday.
"Viscoplast shares have been approved for public trade," Jacek Socha told a news conference after the commission approved 1,956,000 of the firm's shares for trade.
Investors will be able to register for 900,000 shares in Viscoplast, which seeks a parallel market listing.
A 690,000-share large-investor tranche will take place from January 27 to February 5, with investors able to register for up to 65,000 shares.
Small investors will register for 210,000 shares from January 27 to January 31.

Viscoplast President Adam Nowotarski, also present, would not give a prospective issue price but said the majority of the proceeds would go towards modernising production and the firm's power and computer systems.
Viscoplast, one of Europe's largest adhesive bandage makers, made a net profit of 3.6 million zlotys last year on sales of 36 million zlotys.
It netted 0.9 million zlotys over this year's first half on sales of 22.2 million zlotys.
Its main shareholders are National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 11 in Poland's mass privatisation programme, which has 33 percent, and the state treasury, with 25 percent.
